title: Privacy-aware runbook redaction and automated postmortem seeder
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current automated postmortem seeds and runbook attachments pull raw trace spans, logs, and metric slices into Slack/PagerDuty incident cards. Several customers and internal security reviews flagged PII and sensitive configuration data leaking into incident channels. We need a repeatable system that redacts privacy-sensitive content, preserves signal for debugging, and seeds a meaningful postmortem outline and runbook steps automatically when an incident is created.

Goals:
- Build a redaction pipeline that runs before evidence bundling to Slack/PagerDuty and before postmortem seeding.
- Preserve debugging signal (error codes, span context, timing, stack traces as safe abstractions) while removing or tokenizing secrets, keys, user identifiers, and large payloads.
- Produce an initial postmortem draft with sections (timeline, root-cause hypothesis, immediate mitigations, next steps) pre-populated from traces, alerts, and on-call notes.
- Provide a per-customer privacy profile so enterprise tenants can choose stricter redaction or allow more verbose diagnostic content under an opt-in policy.

Scope out of this ticket: building new SSO/KMS integrations, changes to PagerDuty provider contracts, or full UI for privacy profile creation (we will expose a simple flag and defaults).
acceptance_criteria: Redaction pipeline (trace/log/metric extractor) runs as a synchronous pre-send hook for incident evidence payloads and returns a sanitized artifact within 2s for typical incidents
Automated postmortem seed created in incidents with a populated timeline (at least 3 notable events), a one-paragraph hypothesis, and suggested immediate mitigations in >90% of test cases
Enterprise privacy profile toggle applied per-tenant: 'balanced' (default) and 'strict' produce materially different redaction levels in integration tests
No production incidents have unredacted secrets or raw user identifiers in Slack/PagerDuty attachments in a 2-week post-rollout audit for tenants using default profiles
Feature gated behind runtime flag and has a rollback playbook (disable hook + reprocess queue)
work_items: Design redaction rules and taxonomy (PII, creds, config, large payloads, IPs) - collaborate with security
Implement span/log sanitizer library with rule-engine and tokenization support
Add synchronous pre-send hook into evidence-bundler used by Slack and PagerDuty adapters
Create postmortem seeder that maps sanitized artifacts into PRD postmortem template (timeline/hypothesis/mitigations/next-steps)
Add per-tenant privacy profile flag and configuration (two presets for MVP)
End-to-end tests and fuzzing harness to verify redaction coverage and signal preservation
Instrumentation and dashboards: redaction false-positive rate, median hook latency, postmortem seed success rate
Documentation, runbook for rollback, and release notes for SREs and solutions engineers
comments: 2025-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes - agreed to MVP with two privacy presets (balanced/strict). Security to provide initial regexes and negative test corpus.
2025-03-05 - Marco Diaz: Implemented initial sanitizer library with redaction rule engine. Local fuzzing shows 92% of seeded secrets detected, missing some nested JSON keys.
2025-03-07 - Priya Rao (Security): Reviewed ruleset. Suggested adding entropy-based detection for keys and HMAC pattern detection. Will provide updated corpus by 2025-03-10.
2025-03-10 - Marco Diaz: Hook integrated into Slack adapter; created feature flag 'sanitized_evidence_v1'. End-to-end latency measured: median 1.1s, p95 2.7s (needs p95 < 2s target).

2025-03-12 - QA - Ben Cooper: Found regression where large base64 payloads were truncated mid-JSON leading to unparsable artifacts in attachments. Added acceptance test and mitigation (truncate to complete token boundaries).
2025-03-15 - Design Review - Elena Kim: Postmortem seed template approved. Minor wording tweaks on mitigating actions. Asked to include 'confidence' field in hypothesis. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-17 - Marco Diaz: Deployed to staging under feature flag. PagerDuty integration needs size-limited attachments; switching to hosted artifact link pattern to avoid truncation and retain audit trail.
manual_test_plan: 1) Enable feature flag on staging tenant A. 2) Trigger synthetic incident with seeded traces containing PII, API keys, and large payloads. 3) Confirm Slack and PD cards show sanitized evidence (no raw keys), postmortem draft populated, and links to sanitized artifact bucket. 4) Run corpus-driven fuzz tests and verify >95% sensitive tokenized or removed. 5) Validate rollback by disabling flag and ensuring previous behavior resumes without message duplication.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal staging rollout under flag (1 week). Stage 2: Canary to 10% of tenants with default profile for 2 weeks and audit results. Stage 3: Gradual 100% rollout for non-enterprise tenants if audit clear. Enterprise tenants default to 'balanced' but SRE will offer 'strict' on request.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-redaction removes necessary debugging signal. Mitigation: Add rule severity tiers and allow tokenized placeholders that preserve error codes and span IDs.
Risk: Hook adds unacceptable latency. Mitigation: Async fallback with link to queued sanitized artifact and abort to original flow only if latency breaches SLO; instrumentation and p95 alerts.
Risk: False negatives for novel secret formats. Mitigation: Periodic retraining of pattern corpus and add entropy-based heuristics; post-rollout manual review queue.
Risk: PagerDuty/Slack attachment size limits cause truncation. Mitigation: Use hosted sanitized artifact links and generate compact summaries for attachments.
notes_for_support: Support runbook: how to disable sanitized evidence hook, how to reprocess a specific incident for full raw evidence (requires security approval), and steps to escalate a missed-redaction finding to security team.
